s.t: Rivers Cuomo wanted to save it for Weezer’s next album, until producer Ric Ocasek started leaving notes around the studio that read ‘We want Buddy Holly’.
s.src: MusicRadar: the making of Weezer’s Buddy Holly
s.q: Ocasek even took to leaving notes around the studio that read 'We want Buddy Holly'.

s.t: Rivers Cuomo plays heavy-guitar songs ‘real slow’; on tape this one sounded ‘a little dirgy’, so Weezer sped it up during mastering.
s.src: MusicRadar: the making of Weezer’s Buddy Holly
s.q: "We just sped it up during mastering," said Cuomo. ... "It isn't 'til we hear a song back on tape that we realize, 'hey, that's a little dirgy.'"

s.t: Rivers Cuomo first toyed with Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers for the chorus; walking to class, he swapped in Buddy Holly, who wore thick black frames like him.
s.src: Louder: Weezer, the story behind the song Buddy Holly
s.q: He'd initially toyed with using the dancing duo Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, but struggled with the reference points.

s.t: Their label, Geffen, got it onto Microsoft’s Windows 95 CD-ROM without Weezer knowing; Brian Bell, who had no computer, likened what followed to ‘living inside the eye of a hurricane’.
s.src: uDiscover Music: Vevo Footnotes celebrates Weezer’s ‘Buddy Holly’
s.q: the CD-ROM campaign for Microsoft's Windows 95 ... "I didn't have a computer" ... "it was literally like living inside the eye of a hurricane."

s.t: Spike Jonze brought back Al Molinaro, Happy Days’ drive-in owner, to introduce Weezer in the video; 20 years on he had gone grey, so they dyed his hair.
s.src: Los Angeles Times (Mikael Wood): Weezer’s Blue Album at 30
s.q: There's also a newly shot cameo by actor Al Molinaro, who played the drive-in's owner on "Happy Days" ... "It was 20 years later and he was very gray, so we put dye in his hair."

f.t: After a fan’s Twitter campaign for them to cover Toto’s ‘Africa’, they seemed to troll her by covering Toto’s ‘Rosanna’ instead, before finally recording ‘Africa’ too.
f.src: Ultimate Classic Rock: Weezer cover Toto’s ‘Africa’
f.q: Giving in to a fan's social media campaign, Weezer have recorded a version of Toto's 1982 smash ... the band appeared to be trolling her by covering another huge hit from Toto IV, "Rosanna."

f.t: Rolling Stone readers voted their second album, Pinkerton, one of the worst of 1996; in 2002 the magazine’s readers voted it the 16th-greatest album of all time.
f.q: it was voted one of the worst albums of 1996 in a Rolling Stone reader poll. ... in 2002, Rolling Stone readers voted Pinkerton the 16th-greatest album of all time.

f.t: Their singer, Rivers Cuomo, a self-described ‘spreadsheet guy’, keeps years of song ideas in a database he can ask for, say, every idea at 126 BPM in A flat.
f.src: TechCrunch: Rockstar programmer: Rivers Cuomo finds meaning in coding
f.q: "I was always a spreadsheet guy," ... "Hey, show me all the ideas I have at 126 BPM in the key of A flat,"

f.t: They took their name from a nickname Rivers Cuomo’s father gave him, after Wheezer, a character in the Our Gang short films.
f.q: They took their name from a nickname Cuomo's father gave him, which was based on a character called "Wheezer" from the Our Gang short films.

nf.t: Its video shipped on the Windows 95 CD-ROM, and none of the band owned a computer.
nf.q: Geffen did not tell Weezer they had negotiated with Microsoft to include the video; the band members, none of whom owned computers, were oblivious to the implications.
